summary: Platon Oyunsky Yakutsk International Airport (YKS/UEEE) is the primary aviation gateway to the Sakha Republic in eastern Siberia, Russia. Named after Platon Oyunsky, a prominent Yakut writer and statesman, the airport is notable for operating in some of the harshest winter conditions on Earth, with temperatures regularly plunging below -40°C. It serves as a critical lifeline connecting this remote permafrost region to Moscow, other Russian cities, and select international destinations.
faqs:
Q: Why is Yakutsk Airport notable?
A: It is one of the few major airports worldwide that routinely operates in extreme cold conditions, with winter temperatures often falling below -40°C (-40°F).

Q: Who is the airport named after?
A: The airport is named after Platon Oyunsky (1893–1939), a renowned Yakut writer, linguist, and political figure who served as the first chairman of the Yakut ASSR.

Q: What destinations does the airport serve?
A: The airport primarily operates domestic flights to Moscow, St. Petersburg, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk, and other Russian cities, with occasional seasonal international services.

Q: When is the best time to visit Yakutsk?
A: Summer (June–August) offers the most comfortable temperatures, while winter attracts visitors interested in extreme cold experiences and unique cultural festivals.
